title: Invite origin attribution and emergency org-claim remediation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Add deterministic invite origin attribution to audit logs and build an emergency org-claim remediation workflow for customers who lose SSO provisioning or have stale domain verification state. This ticket ties RBAC v2 identities (SSO/SAML assertions and local accounts) to invite events so that admins can trace who initiated membership changes and enables a controlled, auditable path to reclaim an org when invite plumbing fails.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Audit log schema: every org/team invite, accept, and revoke event must record an explicit 'invite_origin' and 'identity_attribution' fields (values: email, invite_link, sso_assertion:IDP_NAME, provisioning_api) and be queryable in Console and exported to our ingestion pipeline.
2) SAML/SSO attribution: when SAML assertions (NameID/email + eduPersonPrincipalName) are used to provision/match users, we persist the assertion id hash and IdP metadata in the audit record while avoiding storing PII (we store hashed identifiers and IdP name).
3) Emergency org-claim workflow: build a limited, auditable flow that allows verified org admins (via multiple attestations) to claim control when primary SSO owners are unreachable and domain verification mismatch prevents invites. Flow must require 2/3 attestations (owner email, billing contact, and support ticket evidence) and generate a policy-scoped audit trail with time-limited admin elevation.
4) Allowlist/denylist reconciliation job: a nightly job that flags pending invites where email domains are on denylist or unverified allowlist, surfaces to Console, and optionally auto-cancels invites per policy.
5) Console UX: admin-facing audit view filter for 'invite_origin' and a step in org-recovery UI that shows required attestations and estimated time-to-complete.
6) Backfill: run a backfill for the past 180 days of invite events to annotate existing audit records where possible (best-effort) and tag ambiguous records as 'origin:unknown' rather than overwrite.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change invite rules themselves (TTL, rate limit thresholds) — those are separate policy config tasks.
- We will not store raw SAML payloads; only short hashed identifiers and metadata.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Attribution granularity: we prefer explicit origin tags over freeform 'notes' so downstream analytics and alerting can rely on a deterministic set of values. However, some historical invites lack enough signals; for those we use 'unknown' and surface a manual investigation link.
- Privacy: to meet compliance and customer privacy we persist only one-way hashes for assertion IDs and redact email local-parts when stored in logs. The IdP display name is stored in plain text for operational clarity.
- Security: emergency-org-claim must be time-limited and gated behind RBAC v2 scope checks; we will implement ephemeral elevation tokens that expire after 6 hours and require audit log entries with the attestation sources.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema: add invite_origin and identity_attribution fields to internal audit proto + migration plan for ES indices.
2) Server: update invite API handlers (invite.create, invite.accept, invite.revoke) to annotate events. Integrate with SSO/SAML middleware to capture assertion hash.
3) Backfill: job that scans audit indices, attempts to infer origin via correlated events (email service webhooks, invite token issuances), and writes annotated records with 'backfilled_by' marker.
4) Emergency flow: new endpoint /orgs/:id/claim that accepts structured attestations, routes through support verification microservice, creates a time-limited admin grant, and emits audit events.
5) Console: new Admin > Security > Invite Audit view and Org > Recovery modal UI. Work with Design for copy and guardrails.
6) Tests: unit tests for schema changes, E2E for emergency flow with staged support stub, load test for backfill to ensure ES indexing rates are acceptable.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What constitutes an acceptable attestation set for emergency claim in regulated customers? (legal input requested)
- Should emergency org-claim produce a billing event/fee? (PM decision)
- Retention policy for the hashed SAML assertion IDs—how long before they are deleted?

comments: 2025-01-15 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after incident INC-2024-2111 where customer lost org access due to stale domain verification. Initial design doc uploaded to Confluence.
2025-01-22 - Arjun Patel: Spike completed. We can capture SAML NameID hash at SSO middleware layer without changing IdP integrations. Prototype PR (7231) shows schema changes and local test harness.

2025-01-30 - Security review (Sofia Ramirez): Reviewed privacy controls. Approved storing only SHA256 hashes of assertion IDs and IdP display names. Confirmed retention should default to 365 days pending legal guidance.

2025-02-03 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Wrote E2E tests for emergency flow using support stub. Found race when backfill writes to ES while indices are reindexing; will add linearizable writes and retry logic.

2025-02-06 - Arjun Patel: Implemented API handlers and Console placeholders. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7428. Need backend sign-off for rollout plan and infra quota for backfill indexing (~2M docs).

2025-02-08 - PM review (Elena Rossi): Prioritized as P1 due to repeated customer impact. Ask: include optional auto-cancel behavior for invites that target denylisted domains; added as follow-up subtask if approved.
2025-02-08 - Next steps: finish PR reviews, schedule security sign-off meeting 2025-02-11, and plan staged rollout to canary orgs for 2 weeks before org-wide launch.
